general.title: Midcaps Hiding 'Historic' AI Bargain: JPMorgan's Leccubarri
general.summary: "This is the second-biggest underperformance in the history of the asset class," JPMorgan Research's Small & Mid-Cap Strategy Global Head Eduardo Leccubarri tells Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie and Skylar Montgomery Koning on "The Opening Trade." He argues that 73% of all AI related stocks are not in any AI traded ETF. For smaller companies, "I think there is a ton of value, unusually so." (Source: Bloomberg)

Zambia Inflation Edges Up on Eve of Interest-Rate Verdict
general.summary: Zambia’s annual inflation rate rose for a second consecutive month in November as a weaker kwacha made imports costlier.

general.title: Rwanda Hikes Key Rate for Fourth Time in Row to Cool Inflation
general.summary: The National Bank of Rwanda raised its key interest rate to its highest level since at least 2009 to contain inflation.

general.title: AI Trade Rebounds in Late Buying Ahead of US Holiday
general.summary: Stocks rose alongside US equity-index futures as investors returned to the artificial intelligence trade in the runup to the Thanksgiving holiday after a week of whipsawing. Bloomberg's Neil Campling has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Taking on Starlink: Europe’s largest satellite factory opens in push to rival Musk
general.summary: The 20,000-square-meter mega factory will be able to produce up to 500 satellites annually, making it the world's third-largest satellite production site.

general.title: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm says
general.summary: Xpeng Co-President Brian Gu shared his humanoid robot predictions with CNBC in an interview Thursday.

general.title: EXCLUSIVE: US chip curbs, distillation crackdown threaten Chinese AI model development, sources say - Reuters
Banks Risk Outages as They Contend With AI Threats
general.summary: The risk of cyberattacks is forcing banks to contend with a growing number of technical hiccups as they race to adapt aging infrastructure and find vulnerabilities before they’re exploited. Artificial intelligence is advancing so fast that IT teams patch first and ask questions later, which can risk outages. Speaking to Bloomberg last week, Citigroup Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser warned of a “tsunami” of patches. Bella Farr reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
